newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares stage post-election rally to end firmer.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares stage post-election rally to end firmer.

text.p: New Zealand shares rallied strongly on Monday to close firmer despite an inconclusive general election on Saturday.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 14.93 points higher at 2,264.47, having been as high as 2,270.28 during the session.
"We've come out of the election and people are just pleased to see the back of it," said Campbell Stewart at SBC Warburg.
"It started with the currency being bought and the bond market rallying strongly, and that's flowed through to the equity market."

New Zealand's financial markets have reacted favourably to the election result, which gave the New Zealand First Party the balance of power between the right and the left. NZ First's decision on which way to lean will determine who forms the next government.
"It might be a centre-left government, but the principles and policies of the structure aren't that wildly different from what we've been living through," Stewart said.
Brokers noted that ratings agency Standard and Poor's had also said it was broadly comfortable with the election outcome.
The leader board was mixed, with Telecom up five at NZ$7.00 and Lion Nathan down two at $3.58.
Elsewhere, rural services group Wrightson rose three cents to a year high of $1.23, and Fletcher Forest jumped 10 cents to $2.33, its highest level in one and a half years.
